key_insight: The sign of a sizable second harmonic in a Josephson junction’s current–phase relation enables distinct superconducting qutrit designs strongly protected against relaxation.
engineering_relevance: Three-junction loops could encode three-level quantum information with protection tailored to material-dependent charge-noise and quasiparticle constraints.
method: Use a positive second harmonic and slight junction asymmetry for a tunable qutrit with an exact charge selection rule.
Use a negative second harmonic and weak symmetry breaking for near charge-noise insensitivity and correctable quasiparticle errors.
Calculate how gate voltage selects the harmonic sign in candidate altermagnetic Josephson junctions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical protection mechanisms and microscopic gate-tuning calculations, but no experimental coherence measurements.
watch_item: Both designs require a sizable second harmonic; dephasing remains limiting, with gate-voltage noise leading in the gate-tuned platform.
paper_title: Noise-Protected Superconducting Qudits from Higher-Harmonic Josephson Junctions
